title: feat(model): decide what a repository's issues and pull requests mean for the board (#16)

body:
## Why

Elliot's central claim is that moving a card *is* the act of execution — one drop merges to a
default branch on github.com. That consequence was a hover tooltip on a 9-point bolt icon.

`evaluateMove` is pure and takes no clock and no I/O, precisely so a view can ask it during
layout. So the board now asks it: **selecting a card turns every column into a labelled
console** stating what moving this card there would run — "Files a GitHub issue", "Asks for
follow-ups, then merges PR 22" — or naming the gap that refuses it, "Story needs a role, a want
and a benefit". The caption comes from the same function `BoardService` commits with, so the
board cannot promise one thing and do another.

## The visual system

Two rules, both encoding what the repo already believes rather than decorating it.

**Monospace means a machine established it** — issue and PR numbers, branches, SHAs, costs,
elapsed times. Proportional is what a human typed. This is `ship the fact, not the prose` (#20)
made typographic.

**Colour is reserved for consequence** — `armed` for a gesture that starts an agent,
`irreversible` for the one that merges, used by exactly one column and one button. Previously a
single `.orange` meant blocked, warning, stalled *and* tool-denial; splitting refusal from
attention gave the palette back its meaning.

## What this fixes

- **`verifiedOutcome` is displayed at last.** Stored since day one, never shown — the app's whole
  epistemology was invisible. Cards now read "Merged as c372f99", "Opened issue #24".
- The card detail sheet becomes an **inspector**, so a run can be watched without covering the
  board. The log went from a 180pt box to a panel that follows new output.
- **Finished logs render like the live tail** instead of raw NDJSON — both go through
  `AppModel.describe`, so a run does not change appearance the moment it ends.
- **Refusals attach to their card** instead of a status line the next message overwrites.
- Cards carried an accessibility button trait with **no activation action** — visible to assistive
  tech and inoperable. Fixed.
- One refusal now has **one sentence**: a disabled repo said "disabled; see Preflight" on the card
  and "switched off in Preflight" in the column caption.
- ⌘→ / ⌘← advance a card; `columnEnteredAt` surfaces as "here 2d"; the five columns share the
  window width instead of leaving Done half off-screen.

## The analysis window (#32)

The same rule carried into the new surface. **`isGrounded` is this feature's `verifiedOutcome`** —
the model calls it "the fastest signal that a story was found rather than invented" and it was
computed and never shown. A proposal now leads with a green seal or a red one, evidence sits in
the fact face as openable chips, and the grounded set is one click.

**Start says what it costs** before it spends it — "Reads the repository 3 times, one run per
lens" — and each lens then reports what it actually ran up.

The six lenses become tiles you arm, and the same strip becomes the live status row. It collapses
once nothing is still reading, and **every alarm survives the collapse**: a run that edited the
repository must not become invisible because the panel it lived in was tidied away.

Also: `dropped` was documented "shown, never swallowed" and lived in a tooltip; raw enum values
reached the user (`completedWithDenials`); two full repository paths side by side ran together
unreadably; and the row actions were hover-only until they gained a context menu and accessibility
actions.

## Verification

There is no CI in this repo, so the gate is local, per `.claude/skills/repo-profile.md`:

- `cd ElliotKit && swift build` — clean
- `cd ElliotKit && swift test` — **408 tests in 52 suites passing**

Changes are confined to `Sources/ElliotApp/`; no shared logic was touched.

Run against a scratch `ELLIOT_HOME` with seeded data, which is how four defects above were found
rather than reasoned about. Two limits worth stating: the drag path was proven only with the
repositories switched off — the drop was received and refused, never allowed to succeed, since a
success would have filed a real issue. And the analysis window's live-progress path is built but
never watched running, because that would spend real money reading the repo six ways.
title: feat(app): say what a gesture will do before it happens

body:
The backlog holds user stories, and until now something had to write them by hand. *Analyze…* reads a registered repository through six lenses — bugs, quick wins, features, tech debt, tests, docs & DX — one `claude -p` run each, and comes back with proposed stories to go through and accept.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-repo-analysis-design.md`
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-05-repo-analysis.md`

## The three decisions worth arguing with

**The artifact is the fact.** There is no `gh` to appeal to about whether a story is a good idea — the agent's judgement *is* the deliverable. So the analogue of "`gh` is the fact" is a file: each run is told to write `stories.json` at a path announced in its own prompt, marked `ELLIOT_OUTPUT=`, and Elliot reads that rather than the closing message. A property test asserts every prompt carries exactly one marker and that it is absolute. If the file is missing the last fenced JSON block is tried, and which source answered is recorded on the run.

**Evidence is resolved, not believed.** Every proposed story must cite `file:line`. Elliot resolves each citation against the repository and confines it there, so a proposal whose files do not exist is shown struck through. It is the only objective fact available about an opinion.

**A run that edits your code is watched for, because it cannot be prevented.** No CLI flag expresses "write, but only under this path". The prompt forbids touching the repository, `--add-dir` makes the scratch directory writable, and `git status --porcelain` is compared before and after.

**Proposals are not cards.** They live in their own table and their own window, so a 30-story analysis does not drown the board and the five columns keep one meaning. Accepting calls the same `BoardService.createCard` the New Card sheet uses. The rule engine, `TriggerAction`, the five columns and the three transitions are untouched.

The same four steps are available over MCP: `board_analyze_repo`, `board_list_proposals`, `board_accept_proposals`, `board_reject_proposals`.

## Merging with main

The branch was cut before `main` gained per-file MCP tools, `RunPage`, `CreatedCard` and the issue #7 process fix, so the merge was not mechanical. Three resolutions were judgement calls, and the merge commit explains each: the analysis migration is renumbered `v4_analysis` because it had shipped nowhere; the protocol version is **3**, since both sides had independently claimed 2 and main's 2 has shipped; and `ProcessRunner` takes this branch's version whole, because it already contains main's fix and adds the pipe-drain ordering and SIGKILL rung main lacks.

The merge also surfaced a defect neither parent had on its own: `TestHome` sets `ELLIOT_HOME` from a lazy static and SwiftPM links every test target into one process, so `RunLogResourceTests` could write a log under one home and read it under another. `TestHome` moved to `TestSupport` and the suite now pins the home before resolving a path.

## Verification

- `swift test` — **408 tests, 52 suites, green**, run four times consecutively (the race above was intermittent, so one green run would not have been evidence).
- `./Scripts/build-app.sh` — `dist/Elliot.app` assembles.
- The whole analysis path is covered end to end without a token or a network call: `Scripts/fake-claude.sh` grew `FAKE_CLAUDE_STORIES` (drop an artifact at the announced path) and `FAKE_CLAUDE_TOUCH` (prove the git sentinel notices a run that edits the repo).

## What is still unproven

**No real repository has been read yet.** Every end-to-end assertion here drives the fake `claude`. The plan's last step — Task 14, Step 3 — is deliberately left unticked: it costs tokens, needs the `.app` launched from the Finder, and is the one thing the fake cannot stand in for. `README.md` says so under Status rather than claiming the feature is proven.
title: feat: read a repository through six lenses and propose user stories

body:
## Problem

A session starting cold in this repository has to read `Package.swift`, `RuleEngine.swift`, `BoardService.swift` and the test suites before it knows which of Elliot's rules are load-bearing. `README.md` explains *why* the design is what it is; nothing states what a contributor must not break.

## Proposed solution

A root `CLAUDE.md` carrying only what is not discoverable from a single file:

- **Commands** — build, test, single-suite filter, format, `build-app.sh`, MCP registration.
- **Architecture** — the layer table that is also the dependency graph, plus the six invariants that each span several targets: the single move funnel through `BoardService`, the single pure rule engine, `ElliotMCPKit` importing neither `ElliotEngine` nor `ElliotProcess`, system moves never triggering skills, `gh` as the fact rather than the agent's prose, and the app as sole writer.
- **Testing discipline** — the three rules that keep `swift test` deterministic and always-terminating, and the matching production rule that nothing waits on `Process.waitUntilExit()`.
- **Things that bite** — additive migrations, the `elliotProtocolVersion` bump, `marketingVersion` as the single version source, captured-not-inherited PATH, main-checkout-only registration, `ELLIOT_HOME`, and the shared `.git` across agent worktrees.

Two omissions are deliberate: no test count (README says 179, `repo-profile.md` says 167, `grep` finds 326 `@Test` attributes — citing any of them without running the suite would be inventing a fact), and no file-by-file listing, which is discoverable.

## Area

None — documentation only, no target touched.

## Verification

Docs-only; no code changed. Note that this repository has **no CI** (no `.github/workflows/`), which the new file records as a fact a contributor needs.
title: docs: CLAUDE.md for working in this repo

body:
Implements the 13 findings of an Elon-style review of the MCP surface, then reconciles them onto #14's one-file-per-tool structure, which landed while this was being written.

## The critical one

`RunDTO` never carried `verifiedOutcome` — the `gh`-established fact the whole verification layer exists to produce. It shipped `resultText` instead, the field `SkillRun` itself documents as *"Display only — never parsed for issue or PR numbers."* So the wire handed the agent the hint and withheld the fact, in a product whose headline decision is "`gh` is the fact; the agent's prose is a hint".

That is not cosmetic: `RunState.succeeded` is compatible with `.noIssueCreated`, `.notMerged` and `.unverified`. **An agent could read "succeeded" on a run that filed nothing and report a merge that never happened.**

It now crosses as a flat tagged DTO whose mapping switch has no `default:`, so a new outcome is a compile error rather than a silent drop. `exitCode`, `stderrPath`, `numTurns` and `isTerminal` travel with it, and `board_move_card`'s description tells the model to judge by it and never by the prose.

## Honest annotations

`board_move_card` merges pull requests, deletes branches and files issues on github.com — and was annotated `destructiveHint: false`, with `openWorldHint` unset. Clients use those hints to decide whether to ask a human first. It is now destructive, open-world and non-idempotent, and its description states the blast radius: `todo → inProgress` spawns an unattended agent with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` in the real checkout.

It is deliberately **not** split into a separate `board_merge`. One gesture is one tool — a second path is what this architecture exists to prevent.

## Two failures that rendered as successes

- Offline, an unknown `repo` filter collapsed to `nil` and returned **every card on the board**, labelled `source: offline-db`, `isError: false`. The live path refused the same call. `listCards` now distinguishes "not requested" from "matched nothing" structurally.
- `encode` swallowed serialisation failures into `.null` and shipped them under `isError: false`, so a bug reached the agent as a well-formed empty answer. The helpers throw now.

A third of the same species turned up during the audit and is fixed here too: a snapshot served because the socket failed was labelled "Elliot is not running" while Elliot was running.

## Closing the gap between the mouse and the agent

Five new tools — `board_update_card`, `board_cancel_run`, `board_list_repos`, `board_await_run`, `board_next`.

`board_await_run` is a long poll, capped server-side, riding a socket whose deadline is deliberately longer than the server's own so the server's timeout is always the one that fires. A timeout returns the run rather than an error, so waiting is never mistaken for failure.

`board_next` is the one that changes what this server is for. The five original tools answered *"what cards exist"*; every one required the caller to already know which card it wanted. `board_next` answers *"what should I do next"* by calling the same pure `evaluateMove` a real move calls — so it predicts the board rather than describing it, and there is no second copy of the transition table.

Paging is honest throughout: `total`, a truncation flag, a server-side cap that says when it bit, and a card order of (repo, column, orderIndex) in board order rather than an `orderIndex` that restarts at 1024 per column.

Run logs and cards are MCP resources now, so the NDJSON transcript is addressable instead of being an undocumented path string.

## Tests

`ElliotMCPKit` had **zero** tests — 167 existed and not one executed a line of the headline feature. It has a target now, behind an injectable bridge, with a regression test per correctness finding. **167 → 302.**

## On the merge with #14

Both changes rewrote `ElliotMCPServer.swift`, in opposite directions. Git reported one conflicted file, which understated it: #14's five `Tools/*.swift` are pure additions and merged in silently beside the monolith — every tool declared twice, `ToolOutput`'s helpers colliding. A clean-looking merge that could not compile.

Resolved as **#14's structure carrying this branch's behaviour**. The registry and its derived dispatch are #14's, so tool names stay written once. The five pre-existing tool files were rewritten rather than patched: they were stale against the new contract in three ways at once — a concrete `AppBridge` where the tests need the protocol, synchronous bridge calls, and the non-throwing encode.

Verified rather than asserted: every one of the ten `Tool(...)` declarations is character-identical to its pre-merge source, so no description sentence or annotation was lost in transit.

## Open, for your call

- `openWorldHint` is `false` on `board_create_card` and `board_update_card` — creating a card reaches nothing; only a later move does. Arguable either way.
- The five new tools have no dedicated tests, only indirect coverage through `ElliotMCPServer`'s public surface. `UpdateCardTool`'s filed-card refusal is the gap I would close first.
- A doc comment in `ElliotMCPServer` says a duplicate tool name is caught at build time; `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` actually traps at first access.
- `ClaudeRunnerTests`' "A final line with no trailing newline is not lost" was reported flaky on a cold `.build` by one auditor. I did not reproduce it in four full runs and `ElliotProcess` is untouched by this branch — passing it on unconfirmed.

The review that produced this is in `reviews/2026-08-05-elon/`, left untracked pending your call on whether it belongs in the repo.

  test` run locally are the only verdict. A minimal CI workflow would make that verdict shared.
- **Design note.** A clone that is on disk and registered but absent from the `gh repo list` answer
  is reported `.ok` with the detail *"On disk; GitHub did not list it."* — a correct-but-quiet
  pairing. If that case matters once the page exists, it may deserve its own verdict rather than
  riding on `.ok`.

body:
Implements #7.

Closes #7.

`swift test` was right about 4 times in 5, and could silently hold the SwiftPM build lock for a
quarter of an hour — which presents as a broken toolchain, not as a stuck test. With no CI in this
repo, that was the only gate before a merge.

### Plan
- [x] Task 1: Capture the actual failure before changing anything
- [x] Task 2: A `TestSupport` target with a bounded `withTimeout`
- [x] Task 3: `fake-claude.sh` never outlives its parent, and signals readiness
- [x] Task 4: Bound and de-flake the `Claude runner` suite
- [x] Task 4b: `ProcessRunner.run` waits the way `StreamingProcess` already does
- [x] Task 5: Bound and de-flake the `End to end` suite
- [x] Task 6: Prove it — 20 consecutive clean runs, and a deliberate wedge

### Task 1 amended the plan, and that is the headline

The spec guessed the flake was `eventsStreamLive`/`cancellation` in `Claude runner`. It was
`cancellingARun` in `End to end`, and it was **not** a wrong exit code — it was `Stack.awaitRun`
expiring, which the planned readiness fix would not have addressed.

Sampling a wedged helper (21 min alive, **no child process**) gave the real cause, in **production**
code:

```
Thread  DispatchQueue_15: com.apple.root.default-qos.cooperative
+ 2370  ProcessRunner.run(…)                      ProcessRunner.swift:66
+   2370 -[NSConcreteTask waitUntilExit]  →  CFRunLoop  →  mach_msg2_trap
```

`RunScheduler.finish` verifies **before** it persists (`RunScheduler.swift:196-198`), so a park in
`verify → GHClient → ProcessRunner.run` means the run row never reaches a terminal state — which is
exactly the 20 s `.timedOut`. One cause, both symptoms. Sampled twice: here, and during `/merge-pr 14`.

So the bounded-test work (Tasks 2–5) was necessary but **not sufficient**, and Task 4b was added —
the one step touching production code. `StreamingProcess.waitForExit` already solves this by
publishing the exit from `terminationHandler` under one lock; `ProcessRunner` never got it. One
funnel, two implementations, only one correct.

Full evidence: [the finding comment](https://github.com/phmatray/Elliot/issues/7#issuecomment-5195701743).

### Evidence

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| 20 consecutive full-suite runs | **20/20 clean**, `179 tests in 18 suites`, 0 wedged |
| Deliberate wedge (`run.cancel()` commented out) | fails in **5.19 s** with `timed out after 5.0s`, not a hang |
| `ClaudeRunnerTests` ×25, post-fix | 25/25 |
| `ProcessRunnerTests` ×15 on **unmodified** `ProcessRunner` | 15/15 — see the caveat below |
| Pristine `main` baseline, `ClaudeRunnerTests` ×25 | 25/25 (so the branch is not worse in isolation) |

⚠️ **The `ProcessRunnerTests` guard never went red.** The wedge is a race and I could not force it on
demand at 40 concurrent children. Its value is that a *reintroduction* fails in seconds instead of
hanging; it is not the evidence that the fix was needed — the sampled stack is.

⚠️ **One failure is disclosed rather than buried.** An early 10-run batch was 9/10: `successfulRun`
saw `events.count → 2` instead of 8 — six stdout lines never reached the decoder, the
`readabilityHandler` vs `readDataToEndOfFile` race that `StreamingProcess.swift:82-96` documents in
its own comment. That batch ran **before** Task 4b landed. Since Task 4b: 20 full-suite runs + 25
filtered runs, all clean. Not proven fixed, and not proven related — stated as measured.

### Two deviations from the plan's code, both because the snippet was wrong

1. **Task 4 Step 3** mutated captured locals inside `withTimeout`'s `@Sendable` operation, which
   `swiftLanguageModes: [.v6]` rejects. Shipped form returns the flags from the closure.
2. **Task 4b Step 3** carried *the very bug it fixes*: it published `exited` and handed off the waiter
   under **two separate locks**, so a waiter parking in between is lost forever. Shipped form uses one
   `Locked<WaitState>`, mirroring `StreamingProcess.State`. Code review then widened the single waiter
   slot to a list, so a future concurrent caller cannot orphan the first waiter either.

### Notes for the reviewer

- **`swift format` was deliberately not run.** `main` itself emits **7714** `swift format lint
  --strict` errors under toolchain defaults (it defaults to 2-space indent; this code is 4-space
  throughout). There is no committed formatter config and no CI, so this is not a gate — running
  `--in-place` would reformat the whole repository and bury the fix. New files add only `[Indentation]`
  findings of that same kind, and contain **zero** lines over 100 chars against 87 on `main`.
- **There is no CI in this repo**, so nothing will run on this PR. The evidence above is local.
- `hang` and `trap` modes of `fake-claude.sh` are now identical; both names are kept because the tests
  read as documentation of intent. Replay mode now traps too, so it can no longer orphan either.

## Follow-ups

- **`ProcessRunner.run` has no SIGKILL escalation.** On timeout it sends SIGTERM only, so a child that
  ignores it parks `withTaskGroup` forever — the same failure class as this issue.
  `StreamingProcess.terminate(hardKillAfter:)` already escalates after 15 s; `ProcessRunner` should too.
- **`ProcessRunner` still blocks two cooperative-pool threads** on
  `Task.detached { readDataToEndOfFile() }` for stdout and stderr. Same family as the bug fixed here
  (blocking calls on the cooperative pool); no evidence yet that it causes failures, so it was left
  alone rather than changed speculatively.
- **`StreamingProcess`'s drain race** — the `successfulRun` truncation above. Worth a bounded
  reproduction attempt before deciding whether it is real.
- **A wedged `swiftpm-testing-helper` from another worktree was observed orphaned (PPID 1)** during
  this work and left alone. If that is a recurring outcome, a cleanup step is warranted.
title: fix(test): bound the fake-claude suites so swift test always terminates (#7)

body:
`create-issue`, `implement-issue` and `merge-pr` read `.claude/skills/repo-profile.md` at their preconditions step. It was missing here, so every run re-derived this repo's build commands, label taxonomy and architecture rules from scratch.

Records what detection proved:

- **Build/test:** `cd ElliotKit && swift build` / `swift test`, single-suite via `--filter`.
- **Integration:** squash on a linear `main`; `<type>(scope): <subject> (#issue)` titles; `feat/<issue>-<slug>` branches — anchored the way `PRMatcher.branchMatches` actually reads them, trailing hyphen included.
- **Labels:** the live set is GitHub's defaults; area lives in the issue body's `## Area` section naming the SwiftPM target, which is what #11 and #12 already do.
- **Architecture grain:** the layer order *is* the dependency graph, `ElliotApp` has no test target so decisions belong further down, `BoardService` is the only writer of `column`, `ElliotMCPKit` imports neither Engine nor Process, and `gh` is the fact.

Three `TODO` markers left rather than invented: there is no CI workflow (nothing runs on a PR, branch protection off), no `priority:`/`effort:` labels, and no committed formatter config — so the format commands are toolchain defaults, not a verified gate.

No source change; documentation only.
title: chore(skills): repo profile for the issue/PR lifecycle skills

body:
ElliotMCPServer.swift held the five tool declarations, their five handlers and the shared rendering helpers in 361 lines. It now holds 69: a registry, the dispatch, and the MCP wiring.

## Layout

```
Sources/ElliotMCPKit/
  ElliotMCPServer.swift   69   registry + dispatch + makeServer()
  BoardTool.swift         22   the protocol: `var tool` + `func call(_:bridge:)`
  ToolOutput.swift        58   CallTool.Result.ok/.failure/.render, Value.encoding
  Tools/
    ListCardsTool.swift   69
    CreateCardTool.swift  90
    MoveCardTool.swift    72
    GetCardTool.swift     45
    ListRunsTool.swift    42
```

## Beyond moving code

**The protocol hands a tool nothing but `AppBridge`.** That is the point rather than a side effect: the README says the helper holds no copy of the rules, and now a tool could not reach around them even if it tried, because nothing else is ever passed to it.

**The dispatch table is derived, not written twice.** The old `switch` listed the five tool names a second time and could drift from the `tools` array. Both now come from one `registry`, so adding a tool is a file plus a line. `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` is deliberate: two tools claiming one name should stop the helper at startup, not silently shadow one of them.

**`Self.ok` / `Self.error` become `.ok` / `.failure` on `CallTool.Result`,** so call sites read `return .failure(code: "bad_argument", ...)`.

## Verification

Behaviour-preserving, and measured rather than assumed. A binary built from the previous commit was compared against this one, with Elliot.app running so replies carried `source: "live"` — the real IPC path, not just the offline fallback:

- `tools/list` — **byte-identical**, including tool order.
- `tools/call` — **identical across three paired runs** for both read tools, an unknown tool, an invalid `card_id`, and a missing one.
- `swift build` clean, no warnings. **167 tests in 15 suites pass.**

One thing worth recording: comparing the raw text first showed two diffs, both of them key *ordering* inside the JSON payload (`{"message":...,"error":...}` versus the reverse). Running the *same* binary six times flips it too — Swift seeds `Dictionary` hashing per process — so it predates this change. The probe parses and re-serialises the payloads before diffing rather than treating that churn as a difference.

No write tool was probed: `board_create_card` and `board_move_card` would have reached the real board.

## Unrelated, but seen while running this

An earlier `swift test` hung for 23 minutes. `sample` put it in `ProcessRunner.run` at `waitUntilExit` (ElliotProcess:66) — a target this PR does not touch, and one no test target reaches through `ElliotMCPKit`. Killed and replayed: green in 1.1 s. Looks like an intermittent flake in the process-spawning tests; not investigated further.
title: refactor(mcp): one file per MCP tool

Implements #5.

Closes #5.

Executing the implementation plan task-by-task; the checklist below — and the plan on the issue — are
ticked as each task lands. Opened as a draft — will be marked ready after the final task and a
code-review pass.

### Plan
- [x] Task 1: `CardDraft` — the editable shape of a card, with its validation rule
- [x] Task 2: `BoardService.updateCard` edits the three fields and refuses a filed card
- [x] Task 3: The detail sheet becomes editable, sharing one field editor with the new-card sheet
      (code complete; the plan's manual GUI pass is still owed — see below)
- [x] Task 4: Document the edit boundary in the README

## Code review

Reviewed over the whole branch. One real bug, fixed in `fix: address code-review findings`:

**Removing the last acceptance criterion left the editor with zero rows** — only in the new detail
sheet, and only because of how it bound the draft. `CardDetailView` passed a hand-rolled
`Binding(get: { draft }, …)` whose getter closed over the *unwrapped local*, so it kept reporting the
pre-mutation value until the body re-evaluated. The remove button mutates twice in one action
(`remove(at:)`, then `if criteria.isEmpty { criteria = [""] }`), so the second read saw a stale
non-empty array and skipped the re-seed — breaking the invariant the plan's own edge-case table
specifies. `NewCardSheet` was unaffected, binding straight to `@State`.

Fixed at both levels: the invariant moved into `CardDraft.removeCriterion(at:)` — one atomic mutation,
in a target `swift test` can actually reach, now covered by 3 tests including a stale-index guard the
original unguarded `remove(at:)` lacked — and `CardDetailView` now uses `Binding($draft)`, which reads
through to the state and removes the whole stale-read hazard. Also: `AppModel.updateCard` returned
failure without setting `status` when the board was nil, so the sheet would have shown an unrelated
leftover message.

## ⚠️ Manual verification still owed

Task 3 Step 7 asks for a click-through in the assembled app. `./Scripts/build-app.sh` runs clean and
`dist/Elliot.app` assembles, but a SwiftUI GUI cannot be driven from a terminal, so **that box is
deliberately left unticked on the issue** rather than claimed. Everything provable by `swift test` is
proven — the two rules this feature turns on (`CardDraft.isValid`, and the engine's filed-card refusal)
live in tested targets precisely because `ElliotApp` has no test target.

Please run, from the Finder (not a shell — the preflight checks exist to survive not inheriting `PATH`):

```
./Scripts/build-app.sh && open dist/Elliot.app
```

- A backlog card with a typo → open → **Edit** offered → fix the `want` → **Save** → sheet returns to
  read-only and the card's narrative updates behind it.
- Blank the label → **Save** greys out.
- Switch a story card to **Plain note**, save, reopen → renders as a note.
- A card showing an `#N` badge → open → no **Edit**, and the sheet reads *"Filed as #N — edit it on
  GitHub. From here on the issue is the record."*

## Follow-ups

- **The `End to end` suite intermittently hangs — pre-existing, and worse than a slow test.**
  Reproduced on unmodified `origin/main` (`677e502`), so it is not caused by this PR, which touches
  no process-spawning code. Two symptoms, same root:
  - *Usually*: exactly one test per run dies at the suite's own 20s `.timedOut`. **Which** test varies
    run to run — `deniedRunIsFlagged`, `crashingRunIsRecorded`, and `cancellingARunStopsIt` have each
    been the casualty; back-to-back runs of the identical command went pass, then fail.
  - *Occasionally*: the test process never exits at all. One `swift test --filter EndToEnd` on pristine
    `main` was still alive after **15 minutes**, holding the SwiftPM build lock and blocking every
    later `swift build` until killed — so a stuck run can look like a broken toolchain.

  Worth a real fix (bounded waits in `Stack.awaitRun`, or `.serialized` on the suite) plus reaping of
  orphaned `fake-claude.sh` children. Verification for this PR was done with repeated runs: the full
  167-test suite passed cleanly twice in a row on the final tree.

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/groue/GRDB.swift/compare/v7.4.1...v7.5.0)

*A new release of the Swift toolkit for SQLite databases.*

#### GRDB 7.5.0 brings a new way to write database requests

```swift
// GRDB 7.4
let count = try Player.filter(Column("score") >= 1000).fetchCount(db)
let players = try Player.order(Column("score")).fetchAll(db)

// NEW with GRDB 7.5.0
let count = try Player.filter { $0.score >= 1000 }.fetchCount(db)
let players = try Player.order(\.score).fetchAll(db)
```

Record types profit from this new syntax if they define a nested `Columns` enum. If you follow the [Recommended Practices for Designing Record Types](https://swiftpackageindex.com/groue/grdb.swift/master/documentation/grdb/recordrecommendedpractices), this `Columns` enum is already defined, and you can profit from the new syntax right away.

With Swift 6.1+, [Table Aliases](https://redirect.github.com/groue/GRDB.swift/blob/master/Documentation/AssociationsBasics.md#table-aliases) have learned to use the `Columns` enum:

```swift
// GRDB 7.4
let authorAlias = TableAlias()
let request = Book
    .joining(required: Book.author.aliased(authorAlias))
    .order(authorAlias[Column("name")], Column("publishDate"))

// NEW with GRDB 7.5.0 and Swift 6.1
let authorAlias = TableAlias<Author>()
let request = Book
    .joining(required: Book.author.aliased(authorAlias))
    .order { [authorAlias.name, $0.publishDate] }
```

#### Breaking Changes

The benefits of this release are so important that two breaking changes were shipped:

- If you define a `public` record type with a nested `Columns` enum, you have to make this enum `public` as well.

  ```diff
   public struct Player: FetchableRecord, PersistableRecord {
  -  enum Columns { ... }
  +  public enum Columns { ... }
   }
  ```

- `TableAlias` is now a generic type. This will break existing code that accepts a `TableAlias` as an argument. You will have to make those methods generic as well.

#### What's Changed

- Make it possible to create a raw FTS5Pattern without any database connection by [@​groue](https://redirect.github.com/groue) in [#​1764](https://redirect.github.com/groue/GRDB.swift/pull/1764)
- Build request with closures by [@​groue](https://redirect.github.com/groue) in [#​1759](https://redirect.github.com/groue/GRDB.swift/pull/1759)

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/groue/GRDB.swift/compare/v7.4.1...v7.5.0>
